government.title: Developmental Humanitarianism: The Rise of Chinese NGOs in Africa and Their Reshaping of the Global Humanitarian Landscape
government.short_title: Developmental Humanitarianism: The Rise of Chinese NGOs in Africa and Their Reshaping of the G…
government.plain_summary: This research examines how Chinese non-governmental organizations (NGOs) are operating in Africa, focusing more on development rather than just providing aid during crises. These NGOs often blend emergency assistance with long-term projects like building local capacities and improving livelihoods. This approach helps them stay relevant by balancing their activities against host countries' sovereignty claims while also aligning with international norms. The study found that these organizations tend to cluster in certain regions, using existing infrastructure for aid and diplomacy.

government.title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
government.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

government.title: Blame Avoidance and Corruption: How Politicians' Denials Shape Citizen Perceptions and Political Accountability
government.short_title: Blame Avoidance and Corruption: How Politicians' Denials Shape Citizen Perceptions and Politic…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how politicians accused of corruption respond when they deny their wrongdoing. The research shows that when politicians say they are innocent or blame others for their actions, it can improve their image and chances of winning elections. This is especially true for people who strongly support one political party. Understanding this helps us see how leaders influence public opinion about corruption in politics.

government.title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy Implications
government.short_title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy I…
government.source: International Journal of Research in Entrepreneurship & Business Studies
government.plain_summary: This study analyzed how airlines handle airfare refunds and the challenges customers face during this process. It found that communication issues are a major problem, especially in understanding airline rules. Despite most customers being satisfied with their refund after receiving one, they felt the process was complex and inefficient. The research suggests clearer policies and better coordination between airlines, intermediaries, and customers could improve trust and service quality.

government.title: Using Open-Source Intelligence and a Top Down/Bottom up Approach to Improve Supply Chain Risk Management in a Government Agency
government.short_title: Using Open-Source Intelligence and a Top Down/Bottom up Approach to Improve Supply Chain Risk…
government.source: International Journal of Value Chain Management

government.title: Strengthening Coastal Resilience through Science-Based Mangrove Governance in Davao Occidental, Philippines
government.short_title: Strengthening Coastal Resilience through Science-Based Mangrove Governance in Davao Occidental…
government.plain_summary: This research highlights that while investing in mangrove restoration in Davao Occidental has been significant, outcomes have varied widely due to issues like incorrect species selection and lack of monitoring. Studies show that by matching the right species to each site and diversifying plant types, survival rates can be very high at over 95%. However, these effective methods are not consistently used because there's no unified policy framework. The study suggests creating a standardized governance system that mandates correct species use, promotes diverse planting strategies, and establishes community monitoring systems supported by partnerships between local governments and universities.

government.title: Machine Learning for Job Matching, Skills Mapping and Labour Market Forecasting in e-Government Systems
government.short_title: Machine Learning for Job Matching, Skills Mapping and Labour Market Forecasting in e-Governmen…
government.source: Journal of Applied Science, Information and Computing
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how advanced machine learning techniques could improve job matching and forecasting in e-government systems used by the Tanzanian government. The main challenges identified were poor usability of the system, weak job skill matching, and lack of real-time updates. Machine learning models helped analyze data better for these issues. The research found that integrating ML into these systems can significantly enhance decision-making, increase efficiency, and match workers with available jobs more accurately.

government.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
government.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
government.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
government.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

government.title: Decoding Moral Vulnerability in AI Environments:A Case Study of Algorithmic Governance and Policy Implications
government.short_title: Decoding Moral Vulnerability in AI Environments:A Case Study of Algorithmic Governance and Pol…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how using AI in professional environments can lead to a situation called "moral vulnerability." This happens when AI systems are used without proper ethical guidelines, which can make people feel uncomfortable or undervalued. The research found that this can cause issues like reduced sense of responsibility and instability in one's role within the organization. To prevent these problems, it suggests several practical steps for leaders to take, such as conducting assessments before using new AI systems, adding some extra steps in user interfaces to slow down decision-making processes, and having independent groups review digital ethics. These suggestions are meant to help protect organizations from potential harm caused by poorly managed AI use.

government.title: Combating Corruption in the Migration Sector: The History and the Present Time
government.short_title: Combating Corruption in the Migration Sector: The History and the Present Time
government.plain_summary: Corruption is widespread in the migration sector, posing significant risks to national security and foreign policy. In Russia, there has been an increase in migration-related crimes, which exposes this area to corruption risks. To combat these issues, it's important to strengthen laws and regulations related to migration, ensuring they are effective against corruption. This can help protect citizens from exploitation and reduce the risk of international conflicts over migration policies.

government.title: AI-based functional expense classification for nonprofit financial reporting and form 990 compliance
government.short_title: AI-based functional expense classification for nonprofit financial reporting and form 990 comp…
government.source: International Journal of Science and Research Archive
government.plain_summary: This study introduces an AI system to automate the process of classifying expenses in financial reports for nonprofits. It uses data from accounting records like P&L details or general ledger along with other inputs like vendor information and payroll records. The AI helps classify direct expenses and allocate shared costs, providing confidence scores and explanations for each classification. This draft report is then reviewed by accountants to ensure accuracy.

government.title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.short_title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.plain_summary: AI is now a key part of how governments make decisions in many areas like healthcare, policing, and welfare. As more AI systems are used, it's important to have rules to make sure they work fairly and don't cause problems. These rules help ensure that AI doesn't lead to unfair treatment or less democracy. By carefully watching how AI is used, we can make sure it helps people and doesn't hurt them.

government.title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
government.short_title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bi…
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on understanding the emotional risks in police work and how they manage their emotions to improve job satisfaction. It was conducted by observing various police units like forensic science, digital investigation, financial division, criminal division, anti-terrorism unit, and more over 26 days. The study found two key emotions that are hard for them to express: interest and frustration. These emotions make it difficult for officers to discuss their work-related feelings openly, leading to invisible or undiscussed labor.

government.title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.short_title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.plain_summary: Data science has become crucial as we generate vast amounts of information daily. It helps transform this data into useful insights for better decision-making across various sectors. For audit institutions, integrating data science can enhance their ability to manage public funds more effectively and improve accountability. By using data science, audits can provide clearer and more accurate reports that recommend improvements faster, which benefits the overall administration and improves citizens' quality of life.

government.title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.short_title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses a scenario where autonomous killer robots are used in warfare without human intervention. These robots can make decisions about who to target based on AI algorithms trained to recognize certain uniforms. If one of these drones targets and kills an enemy soldier who is surrendering, it would violate international laws. Another concern is if the robot makes a mistake by attacking another similar system, leading to unintended conflicts.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.title: The Boundaries of Criminal Liability of Cooperative Management and Cooperatives as Corporations in Corruption Crimes
government.short_title: The Boundaries of Criminal Liability of Cooperative Management and Cooperatives as Corporation…
government.source: International Journal of Sociology and Law
government.plain_summary: This study examines how cooperatives can be held responsible for corruption crimes. It shows that while individual managers of cooperatives may face charges if they misuse their power or benefit personally from wrongdoing, cooperatives themselves are only liable when their policies lead to losses, provide benefits to the organization, or indicate failures in internal oversight. The research aims to clarify these responsibilities and improve legal frameworks to better combat corruption within cooperative sectors. This clarity helps ensure that both individuals and organizations can be held accountable appropriately, leading to more effective law enforcement against corruption.

government.title: Technologization of Anti-Corruption Policy and Changes in the Procedure for income control
government.short_title: Technologization of Anti-Corruption Policy and Changes in the Procedure for income control
government.plain_summary: Anti-corruption policies aim to prevent corruption by identifying individuals who might be involved. In Russia, this has changed from annual reports filled out manually to focusing on specific areas like personnel decisions and property transactions. Now, there's a digital platform that monitors these activities in real-time using objective data from various sources. This helps catch any discrepancies or hidden assets quickly.

government.title: Rule of Law or Rule of Politics? Understanding Varieties of Judicial Anti-Corruption Campaigns
government.short_title: Rule of Law or Rule of Politics? Understanding Varieties of Judicial Anti-Corruption Campaigns
government.source: Annual Review of Law and Social Science
government.plain_summary: This study looks at anti-corruption efforts by judges and prosecutors targeting powerful politicians. It finds these campaigns are often political moves rather than purely legal actions. They can either strengthen fair governance or just look good without changing anything real. The effectiveness varies widely depending on how open the process is, what kind of government they're in, and if it leads to less corruption or other problems like people losing trust in leaders.

government.title: Responsibility of the Company's Board of Directors as Perpetrators of Corruption Crimes in Case Decision Number: 17/Pid.Sus-Tpk/2020/Pn.Plk
government.short_title: Responsibility of the Company's Board of Directors as Perpetrators of Corruption Crimes in Cas…
government.source: International Journal of Social Service and Research
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how Indonesia’s law treats corruption cases involving corporations. A company owner named Didie was found guilty of corruption for a road project. The research shows that even though companies are legal entities, they can still be held responsible if their actions lead to corruption. This means the company itself and not just its owners could be punished.

government.title: Institutional Quality and the Corruption-Growth Nexus: A Panel Data Analysis for Developing Countries
government.short_title: Institutional Quality and the Corruption-Growth Nexus: A Panel Data Analysis for Developing Co…
government.source: Journal of Innovative Research and Technology
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how strong institutions in developing countries affect corruption and economic growth. It uses data from 23 Asian countries over many years. The main finding is that when there's less corruption, economies grow better. Stronger institutions help reduce corruption’s negative impact on growth.

government.title: Assessing the Effectiveness of E-Governance in Enhancing Transparency and Accountability in Public Secondary Schools in Nairobi County, Kenya
government.short_title: Assessing the Effectiveness of E-Governance in Enhancing Transparency and Accountability in Pu…
government.source: Journal of Education Management and Leadership (JEML)
government.plain_summary: This research aimed to see how digital tools help keep schools in Nairobi County, Kenya, more transparent and accountable with their money. They looked at 39 schools and interviewed various people like school leaders, accountants, and officials. The study found that using these digital tools did make things better, but there were some challenges like not enough computers or training for staff. To improve this, they suggest making sure all schools have good technology, giving teachers more training, having help with tech issues, being careful about keeping information safe from hackers, and the government checking everything regularly.

government.title: Analysis Of Transparency and Accountability In Local Government Management And Its Implications For Public Service Performance In West Sulawesi
government.short_title: Analysis Of Transparency and Accountability In Local Government Management And Its Implication…
government.source: Journal of Business and Management Inaba
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how much information is shared about government actions (transparency) and how well they follow rules (accountability) affects how good services are provided by local governments in West Sulawesi. It found that when more people know what the government does and see it follows its duties, public services improve. The findings suggest that making sure the government acts fairly and openly helps them do a better job of providing services to citizens. This means transparency and accountability lead to higher-quality public service delivery.

government.title: Animal anti-rabies vaccination coverage, Upper West Region, Ghana, 2024
government.short_title: Animal anti-rabies vaccination coverage, Upper West Region, Ghana, 2024
government.source: Journal of Interventional Epidemiology and Public Health
government.plain_summary: In Ghana's Upper West Region, there has been a low uptake of anti-rabies vaccinations for dogs and other animals like cats and monkeys. From 2019 to 2023, about 32,874 animals were vaccinated against rabies, with most being dogs (86.9%). The lowest vaccination rate was for monkeys at just 0.1%. Lambussie district had the highest number of vaccinated animals, while Sissala West district had the fewest.

government.title: International Anti-Corruption Commissions: Explaining Institutional Design and Autonomy
government.short_title: International Anti-Corruption Commissions: Explaining Institutional Design and Autonomy
government.plain_summary: Political corruption is a big problem that governments often struggle with and sometimes use anti-corruption measures against their own democracy. International Anti-Corruption Commissions (IACCs) help address this issue by working with both international experts and local people. Some IACCs have more independence than others, which can affect how effective they are in fighting corruption. In places like northern Central America, when there are coalitions that include government insiders and activists at the table during negotiations, these groups use their influence to make sure anti-corruption efforts don't undermine democracy too much.

government.title: Diagnostic Significance of Combining Anti-Gliadin IgA and Anti-Tissue Transglutaminase IgA in Suspected Celiac Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study
government.short_title: Diagnostic Significance of Combining Anti-Gliadin IgA and Anti-Tissue Transglutaminase IgA in…
government.plain_summary: This study looked at a group of 384 people who might have Celiac Disease. They tested these people for two antibodies: one against gliadin (anti-gliadin IgA) and another against tissue transglutaminase (anti-tTG IgA). About 13% had the anti-gliadin antibody, while about 15% had the anti-tTG antibody. When both were positive in some people, it was more common than just one being positive.

government.title: The Transparency Paradox: How Digital Accountability Can Inflate Public Costs in Low-Trust Environments
government.short_title: The Transparency Paradox: How Digital Accountability Can Inflate Public Costs in Low-Trust Env…

government.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Transparency, and Public Service Delivery
government.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Tran…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how artificial intelligence is being used in government services. It found that while AI can speed up service delivery and improve monitoring of processes, it also creates issues like unclear responsibility for decisions made by AI systems, lack of transparency about these decisions, uneven readiness among staff to use AI, and risks to human decision-making. To address these challenges, the study recommends creating clear guidelines on accountability, making AI explanations transparent, encouraging public disclosure, ensuring human oversight over AI processes, providing training for staff, and offering ways for citizens to appeal if they have concerns about AI decisions.

government.title: Beyond Compliance: Building Financial and Anti-Fraud Resilience in the Digital Economy
government.short_title: Beyond Compliance: Building Financial and Anti-Fraud Resilience in the Digital Economy
government.plain_summary: Building financial and anti-fraud resilience is crucial for organizations to maintain stability and public trust in a digital economy. Fraud has evolved into sophisticated forms like cyber-enabled fraud, identity theft, and cryptocurrency scams, requiring more than just compliance measures. To prevent, detect, respond to, and recover from these threats, institutions need integrated governance, control systems, intelligence gathering, response mechanisms, and learning processes. Effective resilience includes board oversight, strong authentication, internal controls, transaction monitoring, whistleblower channels, anti-money laundering integration, incident response plans, customer protection, and post-incident reviews.

government.title: Valuation Methods for Assessing Government-Owned Heritage Buildings in Malaysia
government.short_title: Valuation Methods for Assessing Government-Owned Heritage Buildings in Malaysia
government.source: IPN Journal of Research and Practice in Public Sector Accounting and Management
government.plain_summary: This study aimed to find suitable methods for valuing government-owned historic buildings in Malaysia. It used focus group discussions with experts from various fields like architecture and conservation. The research concluded that these buildings should be valued using a cost approach, focusing on their reproduction costs rather than assigning them a low value of RM1. This ensures compliance with the Malaysian Public Sector Accounting Standards (MPSAS).

government.title: The Defects of "Zeroing" in WTO Anti-Dumping Agreement and Legislative Amendment
government.short_title: The Defects of "Zeroing" in WTO Anti-Dumping Agreement and Legislative Amendment
government.source: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
government.plain_summary: Zeroing is a controversial practice in World Trade Organization (WTO) anti-dumping laws where authorities set negative dumping margins to zero when calculating overall dumping rates. This artificially inflates final duty rates. The WTO Appellate Body has ruled this inconsistent with core provisions of the Anti-Dumping Agreement, but it still persists due to legal ambiguities and protectionist incentives. To address these issues, there should be clear prohibitions, standardized calculation methods, and stronger enforcement mechanisms in legislation.

government.title: From Corruption to Declining Public Trust: Implications for Political Participation in West Aceh Regency
government.short_title: From Corruption to Declining Public Trust: Implications for Political Participation in West Ac…
government.plain_summary: Corruption significantly impacts the level of public trust in West Aceh Regency's governance, affecting both elected and non-elected institutions. Citizens view corruption as a lack of accountability and transparency, using public resources unfairly. This perception leads to declining trust in government bodies. To improve this situation, it’s important to strengthen formal accountability, transparency, and oversight mechanisms.

government.title: Fostering Public Trust and Accountability in Public Healthcare: The Role of Transparency, Integrity, and Independence in Internal Audit Governance
government.short_title: Fostering Public Trust and Accountability in Public Healthcare: The Role of Transparency, Inte…
government.source: European Journal of Social Science Education and Research
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how transparency, independence, and integrity help improve internal audits in public healthcare. It found that having clear information and being free from bias are important for good audits. However, strong ethical values alone don't make a big difference to audit quality. Instead, they play a crucial role when there is also trust and fairness in the system.

government.title: Public Procurement's Long COVID : Emergency Responses and Shifting Corruption Risks in Europe
government.short_title: Public Procurement's Long COVID : Emergency Responses and Shifting Corruption Risks in Europe
government.plain_summary: This study examines how the public procurement system in Europe was affected during the pandemic. It found that spending on coronavirus-related projects led to an increase in corruption risks, especially in countries where government controls are not very strict. This happened because new companies without experience dealing with COVID-19 products took advantage of weak regulations to win big contracts. The study also noted that this increased risk spread beyond just healthcare procurement into other areas like general public services.

government.title: Nursing students' perceptions of an anti-stigma intervention for schizophrenia: a qualitative focus group study
government.short_title: Nursing students' perceptions of an anti-stigma intervention for schizophrenia: a qualitative…
government.plain_summary: This study aimed to understand how nursing students felt about a program designed to reduce stigma around schizophrenia. It found that participating in this program was seen as easy to do, helpful for people who need it, and effective at changing attitudes. The students also gave suggestions on how the program could be made even better. This information can help make future programs more useful for health professionals like nurses.

government.title: Innovation entry as governance filter: shaping exploratory digital innovation in the public sector
government.short_title: Innovation entry as governance filter: shaping exploratory digital innovation in the public se…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how the way government organizations handle new ideas affects their ability to try out innovative technologies and approaches. Many public sector groups are used to solving problems step-by-step, but this can make it hard to explore new ideas freely. The research found that the rules for starting and moving through innovation projects act like filters, often pushing exploratory work towards more traditional ways of working. This means they tend to focus on quick fixes rather than experimenting with different solutions.

government.title: How ethical leadership reduces corruption in Pakistan’s public sector: job satisfaction as a mediator
government.short_title: How ethical leadership reduces corruption in Pakistan’s public sector: job satisfaction as a m…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how ethical leadership can reduce corruption among public employees in Pakistan. It found that when leaders are ethical, it leads to higher job satisfaction for their staff. Higher job satisfaction then reduces the likelihood of corruption by making workers feel more committed to serving the public. This study suggests that if managers promote ethical behavior and boost employee happiness, they can help prevent corrupt practices in government.

government.title: Ethical and Legal Implications of AI-Driven Anti-Corruption Technologies in Developing Democracies
government.short_title: Ethical and Legal Implications of AI-Driven Anti-Corruption Technologies in Developing Democra…
government.source: African Journal of Law Political Research and Administration
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how AI can help spot fraud in government spending in countries that are just starting to have democratic systems. It suggests that using AI like machine learning could make it easier for people to see if money is being spent unfairly or wasted. However, there are still big challenges like not having enough good data or fair rules. The main idea is that while AI can be useful, it needs to work with human checks and balances to really help stop corruption.

government.title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
government.short_title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
government.source: Journal of Social Politics and Governance (JSPG)
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how different groups like governments, businesses, non-profits, schools, and media work together to fight corruption using something called the Pentahelix framework. It found that for effective anti-corruption efforts, these groups need to collaborate closely rather than working separately. The Pentahelix model shows they can tackle corruption more effectively when they all play a part in it. This collaborative approach is key to creating strong systems against corruption and making sure it doesn't happen anymore.

government.short_title: Local Government Transparency and Citizen Satisfaction: Examining the Role of Public Trust and…

government.title: A Study on the Use of Blockchain Technology to Prevent and Detect Corruption in Thailand's Government Procurement Process
government.short_title: A Study on the Use of Blockchain Technology to Prevent and Detect Corruption in Thailand's Gov…
government.source: International Journal of Electronic Government Research
government.plain_summary: This research suggests using blockchain technology to help stop corruption in government buying things. It found that having a good understanding of how to use blockchain is still not common among Thai governments. The study recommends creating new systems with blockchain like smart contracts and online training programs to make sure everyone follows rules fairly during the buying process. This can improve trust between buyers, sellers, and officials.

government.title: Governing Algorithmic Fairness in Climate-Health Systems: A Policy Framework for Bias Mitigation in Public Sector Decision-Making
government.short_title: Governing Algorithmic Fairness in Climate-Health Systems: A Policy Framework for Bias Mitigati…
government.source: Journal of Public Policy and Local Government (JPPLG)
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how artificial intelligence is being used to help make decisions about climate and health issues in government. While this technology can be very useful, it also has the potential to unfairly treat certain groups of people if not managed properly. The paper introduces a new framework called AFCHG that helps governments use AI fairly when making these kinds of decisions. This framework includes four main parts: setting rules, ensuring fair decision-making processes, fixing any unfairness in how AI works, and considering fairness for all people.

government.title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCATION IN ENCOURAGING SUSTAINABLE GLOBAL ECONOMIC RECOVERY IN THE ERA OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
government.short_title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCA…
government.source: International Journal of Law Government and Communication
government.plain_summary: Digital transformations have made using visuals an important part of how Public Relations communicates information. This helps educate people about things like sustainable economic recovery. But with more use of digital visuals comes new rules and ethical standards to follow. Our research looked at these issues, finding that following good ethics and staying within legal guidelines is key for effective PR communication.

government.title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA)
government.short_title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering…
government.plain_summary: Money laundering is a significant threat affecting competitive markets, security, and consumer well-being. The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA) was created as part of new EU regulations to improve supervisory standards and coordinate the fight against illicit finance across Europe. AMLA combines classification functions like setting rules and standards with selective enforcement tools such as direct supervision of high-risk groups and escalation mechanisms. By viewing these aspects through a collective-action lens, it helps explain how AMLA can effectively police money laundering while also highlighting its limitations in fully addressing the issue.

government.title: Development of Anti-Corruption Declaration in Russia: Legal Aspects and Contemporary Challenges
government.short_title: Development of Anti-Corruption Declaration in Russia: Legal Aspects and Contemporary Challenges
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how Russia is making rules for people to declare if they have done anything wrong that could be seen as corrupt. In recent years, it's gotten more complicated how this works. On one hand, there are now better ways for government to check on people who might be doing bad things and use computers more. But on the other hand, fewer people can easily see these declarations because the government says they need to protect everyone from danger.

nonprofit.title: Developmental Humanitarianism: The Rise of Chinese NGOs in Africa and Their Reshaping of the Global Humanitarian Landscape
nonprofit.short_title: Developmental Humanitarianism: The Rise of Chinese NGOs in Africa and Their Reshaping of the G…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research examines how Chinese non-governmental organizations (NGOs) are operating in Africa, focusing more on development rather than just providing aid during crises. These NGOs often blend emergency assistance with long-term projects like building local capacities and improving livelihoods. This approach helps them stay relevant by balancing their activities against host countries' sovereignty claims while also aligning with international norms. The study found that these organizations tend to cluster in certain regions, using existing infrastructure for aid and diplomacy.

nonprofit.title: The Ethics of Islamic Philanthropy
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study about Islamic philanthropy uses Quranic teachings to understand the ethics behind giving. It identifies four key principles: being responsible (amanah), improving oneself (tazkiyah), sharing with others in cycles (dawr), and giving back as a way of receiving (mukāfa’ah). These principles form a strong moral foundation for Islamic charity, showing it's not just about voluntary acts but also includes duties. This research helps clarify how these ethical guidelines affect the structure and diversity within nonprofit organizations.

nonprofit.title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
nonprofit.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
nonprofit.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

nonprofit.title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy Implications
nonprofit.short_title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy I…
nonprofit.source: International Journal of Research in Entrepreneurship & Business Studies
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study analyzed how airlines handle airfare refunds and the challenges customers face during this process. It found that communication issues are a major problem, especially in understanding airline rules. Despite most customers being satisfied with their refund after receiving one, they felt the process was complex and inefficient. The research suggests clearer policies and better coordination between airlines, intermediaries, and customers could improve trust and service quality.

nonprofit.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
nonprofit.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
nonprofit.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
nonprofit.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

nonprofit.title: AI-based functional expense classification for nonprofit financial reporting and form 990 compliance
nonprofit.short_title: AI-based functional expense classification for nonprofit financial reporting and form 990 comp…
nonprofit.source: International Journal of Science and Research Archive
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study introduces an AI system to automate the process of classifying expenses in financial reports for nonprofits. It uses data from accounting records like P&L details or general ledger along with other inputs like vendor information and payroll records. The AI helps classify direct expenses and allocate shared costs, providing confidence scores and explanations for each classification. This draft report is then reviewed by accountants to ensure accuracy.

nonprofit.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Transparency, and Public Service Delivery
nonprofit.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Tran…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research looks at how artificial intelligence is being used in government services. It found that while AI can speed up service delivery and improve monitoring of processes, it also creates issues like unclear responsibility for decisions made by AI systems, lack of transparency about these decisions, uneven readiness among staff to use AI, and risks to human decision-making. To address these challenges, the study recommends creating clear guidelines on accountability, making AI explanations transparent, encouraging public disclosure, ensuring human oversight over AI processes, providing training for staff, and offering ways for citizens to appeal if they have concerns about AI decisions.

nonprofit.title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
nonprofit.short_title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
nonprofit.source: Journal of Social Politics and Governance (JSPG)
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how different groups like governments, businesses, non-profits, schools, and media work together to fight corruption using something called the Pentahelix framework. It found that for effective anti-corruption efforts, these groups need to collaborate closely rather than working separately. The Pentahelix model shows they can tackle corruption more effectively when they all play a part in it. This collaborative approach is key to creating strong systems against corruption and making sure it doesn't happen anymore.

nonprofit.title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCATION IN ENCOURAGING SUSTAINABLE GLOBAL ECONOMIC RECOVERY IN THE ERA OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
nonprofit.short_title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCA…
nonprofit.source: International Journal of Law Government and Communication
nonprofit.plain_summary: Digital transformations have made using visuals an important part of how Public Relations communicates information. This helps educate people about things like sustainable economic recovery. But with more use of digital visuals comes new rules and ethical standards to follow. Our research looked at these issues, finding that following good ethics and staying within legal guidelines is key for effective PR communication.

nonprofit.title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesian Governance
nonprofit.short_title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesi…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how ethics, accountability, and transparency work together in Indonesian government systems. It found that even with digitalization efforts, if there isn't a strong enough foundation of ethics, these measures can fail to prevent corruption and lose public trust. The research suggests integrating ethical practices, making information transparent, and ensuring accountability are all important for effective governance. By combining these elements, Indonesia can improve its government systems and build more trustworthy relationships with the people it serves.

nonprofit.title: CHALLENGES AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF UKRAINE’S STATE ANTI-CORRUPTION BODIES
nonprofit.short_title: CHALLENGES AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF UKRAINE’S STATE ANTI-CORRUPTION B…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This article discusses key issues facing Ukraine's anti-corruption bodies and suggests ways to improve their effectiveness. Challenges include fragmented legal support, political instability, lack of coordination among agencies, limited resources, unclear jurisdictional powers, and low public trust. To address these, the Ukrainian government should focus on strengthening institutional independence, optimizing power distribution, improving human resources, enhancing coordination mechanisms, and increasing transparency in sensitive areas like procurement and financial controls. These steps are crucial for building trust with society and aligning anti-corruption efforts with European standards of governance.
